notes.summary: Constructed an explicit proper smooth analytic torus quotient and proved an integral-period obstruction. Actual nonalgebraizability remains uncertified: the line-bundle classification and arbitrary-algebraization bridge were not fully audited.
notes.detailedSummary: Over K=C((s)), with |s|=exp(-1/8) and t=s^8, the lattice generated by (t,2) and (3,t) acts freely and properly discontinuously on (G_m^2)^an. Ordinary open analytic gluing constructs a good strict, separated, proper, boundaryless, geometrically connected smooth surface. Exact character symmetry forces every period matrix to be [[0,k],[k,0]], which is never positive definite. This proves the explicitly defined period obstruction, including rational coefficients after clearing denominators, but does not independently exclude every scheme or algebraic-space algebraization.
notes.text:
Retained hypotheses and construction. Let K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, and v=-log|·|, so v(t)=1. This is a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of characteristic and residue characteristic zero. Let T=(G_m^2)^an_K, with coordinates z_1,z_2. Set λ_1=(t,2), λ_2=(3,t), and λ(n)=(t^{n_1}3^{n_2},2^{n_1}t^{n_2}) for n∈Z². For x_j=-log|z_j|, multiplication by λ(n) changes x to x+n.

Existence and geometry of the analytic quotient. If B⊂R² is an ordinary open rectangle with side lengths less than one, U_B=trop^{-1}(B) is disjoint from every nonidentity lattice translate. Consequently its image in the set quotient is an ordinary open chart. Overlap identifications are analytic coordinate multiplications by λ(n), and satisfy the cocycle identity λ(n+m)=λ(n)λ(m). Gluing these ordinary open analytic charts constructs X=T/Λ and its analytic sheaf; the projection is a topological covering and local analytic isomorphism.

For compact C,D⊂T, an intersection λ(n)C∩D requires n∈trop(D)-trop(C), a bounded set containing only finitely many integer vectors. Relatively compact neighborhoods and separation of these finitely many translations separate distinct orbits, so X is Hausdorff. The analytic equivalence relation is a locally finite union of closed translation graphs; in the disjoint-sheet charts the diagonal is a closed immersion. Thus X is analytically separated. The compact strict polyannulus |t|≤|z_j|≤1 surjects onto X, establishing compactness. Local charts are ordinary opens of the analytic torus, establishing smoothness, pure dimension two and absence of relative boundary. Strict affinoid neighborhoods are obtained using tropical rectangles with grid endpoints in (1/8)Z, chosen with the point in their central half. Hence X is good and strict. Compactness, separatedness and empty relative boundary establish properness. Integral Laurent-series algebras make the exhausting polyannuli connected; the same argument survives complete field extension. The quotient is therefore geometrically connected.

There is a continuous tropical map τ:X→S=R²/Z² and a closed Gauss section i:S→X. On T, the Gauss norm at x is η_x(Σ_m a_m z^m)=max_m |a_m|exp(-m·x). Its associated graded Laurent algebra is integral, giving multiplicativity. Evaluation gives continuity. Translation by λ(n) sends η_x to η_{x+n}, so the section descends. Since τi is the identity and S is compact while X is Hausdorff, its image is closed.

Universal elementary period obstruction. Explicitly define a positive integral period form to mean a homomorphism c:Λ→Z² satisfying λ_j^{c(λ_i)}=λ_i^{c(λ_j)}, with B_ij=v(λ_j^{c(λ_i)}) positive definite. Write c(λ_1)=(a,b), c(λ_2)=(c,d). Symmetry is 3^a t^b=t^c2^d. Valuation gives b=c. The remaining equality 3^a=2^d forces a=d=0 by unique prime factorization, including negative exponents after clearing denominators. Thus c(λ_1)=(0,k), c(λ_2)=(k,0) and B=[[0,k],[k,0]]. For k≠0 the eigenvalues have opposite signs; for k=0 the matrix vanishes. Neither sign convention gives positive definiteness. Clearing denominators proves the corresponding rational obstruction. Field extension does not change these identities between elements of K.

Limitation decisive for P16.7. This is a proof of the stated period condition's failure, not a certified theorem excluding every algebraization. CLD Appendix B.6 states the analytic line-bundle descent classification and ampleness criterion but defers essential proofs to Lütkebohmert, Section 6.2 and Theorem 6.4.4. Those complete immediate proofs were not retrieved. An arbitrary algebraization additionally requires an audited proper-GAGA descent of the analytic group law, followed by projectivity/polarization of the resulting proper connected algebraic group and applicability of the period classification. Absence of one equivariant polarization cannot substitute for these steps. The example is an explicit candidate for the nonalgebraizable route, with that original quantifier still missing.

Complete arguments are in P16.7-paper.tex and whole-proof.md; application boundaries are in source-application-ledger.md. The bounded diagnostic independently enumerated all 6,561 tuples in [-4,4]^4 and found exactly (0,k,k,0), k=-4,…,4. This exhaustive finite observation does not prove the universal result; the prime-factor argument above does. Reproduce the diagnostic with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`. These are unverified mathematical drafts within the stated standard Berkovich foundational setting.

notes.summary: Constructed genuine bounded mixed CLD products of raw mass two, with comparison, on the quotient. An explicit continuous potential has an MA atom of mass one outside its canonical skeleton; this rules out unrestricted invariant reduction.
notes.detailedSummary: The positive real datum θ=d'd''((x_1²+x_2²)/2) descends globally, with θ²=2i_*Lebesgue. On the explicitly restricted class C_θ of continuous potentials whose local weights admit uniform smooth positive-Hessian approximations, recursive CLD products are positive, symmetric, local, uniformly continuous and have mass two. They satisfy comparison. A local logarithmic-max perturbation places an atom of mass one at the Gauss point of |z_j−1|≤exp(-1), outside i(S). This is an actual analytic measure calculation, not merely a tropical pushforward. It provides no unbounded finite-energy extension or full psh recognition.
notes.text:
Use the analytic quotient, tropical map and Gauss section proved in n1. Put q(x)=(x_1²+x_2²)/2 and θ=d'd''q. A deck translation changes q by n·x+|n|²/2, a smooth real affine logarithmic function with zero Hessian. Hence θ is a globally defined closed positive ordinary CLD (1,1)-form. It is a real differential datum; no ample algebraic/formal line bundle, strict positivity in every analytic direction, or equivalence with classical, weak-smooth or BFJ model psh is asserted.

Normalization. With positive interleaved volume dV=d'x_1∧d''x_1∧d'x_2∧d''x_2, exterior algebra gives (d'd''F)²=2 det(D²F)dV. The identity coordinate moment has analytic degree one and saturated tangent lattice Z². Its canonical calibration is therefore one. CLD integration gives θ²=2i_*(dx_1dx_2) on the unit square modulo translations, so the raw mass is two.

Bounded domain and genuine operator. Define C_θ to consist of real continuous u on X such that q+u is locally a uniform limit of ordinary CLD-smooth functions with positive Hessian. This is intrinsic relative to θ because changes of lift have smooth zero Hessian. It is not declared to be the full analytic psh cone or E¹. Let α_u=θ+d'd''[u]. Locally define its mixed measure with α_v by d'd''((q+u)d'd''(q+v)). Positive currents have order zero, so continuous multiplication is legitimate. If positive T_j→T and continuous f_j→f locally uniformly, choose a smooth g uniformly close to f on a compact test neighborhood and write f_jT_j−fT=(f_j−g)T_j+g(T_j−T)+(g−f)T. Positive-test domination bounds the first and last terms by the approximation error, while the middle tends to zero. This proves f_jT_j→fT. Recursion then proves positivity, closedness and uniform continuity of Hessian products; simultaneous smooth approximation proves symmetry. Smooth zero-Hessian changes of local potentials leave the products unchanged, so they glue globally.

The global identity is α_u∧α_v=θ∧α_v+d'd''(uα_v), and θ∧α_v=θ²+d'd''(vθ). Pairing exact currents with the smooth constant one gives zero. Thus every mixed measure has mass two. Positive top currents are Radon measures, and smooth-test density turns current convergence into weak measure convergence. Decreasing continuity follows by Dini when the limit is continuous and belongs to C_θ; no continuity toward unbounded limits is proved.

Comparison proof. Smooth convex regularized maxima show that C_θ is stable under maximum. Set w=max(u,v−ε). Locality and total mass yield MA_θ(v){u<v−ε}≤2−MA_θ(u){u>v−ε}=MA_θ(u){u≤v−ε}. Let ε decrease to zero and use continuity from below on both sets. Consequently MA_θ(v){u<v}≤MA_θ(u){u<v} for all u,v∈C_θ.

Actual analytic branch example. Let G(y)=y²/2−y/2+1/12 on [0,1], extended periodically, h_0=−G, and u_0=h_0(x_1)+h_0(x_2). Near zero, q+u_0=(|x_1|+|x_2|)/2−1/6. Its genuine MA is 2δ_{i(0)}, as independently calculated in n3. On the sheet V given by |x_j|<1/4, take r=exp(-1), b_j=log max(1,|z_j|), ℓ_j=log max(r,|z_j−1|), and D=max(ℓ_1−b_1,ℓ_2−b_2). Extend D by zero outside V. Ultrametricity gives ℓ_j−b_j≤0, with equality whenever |z_j|≠1. Thus D can be nonzero only in the compact tropical-zero fiber inside V, making its extension continuous. Set U=u_0+D.

A local weight is max(ℓ_1+b_2,b_1+ℓ_2)−(1/2)log|z_1z_2|−1/6. Each logarithmic maximum has uniform smooth psh approximations: near z_j−1=0 it is constant; elsewhere its nonconstant logarithm is an invertible analytic coordinate. Convex regularized maxima and sums preserve positive Hessian. Therefore U∈C_θ and its raw MA mass is two.

On the ordinary open branch W where |z_j−1|<1, set w_j=z_j−1. The local weight becomes log max(r,|w_1|,|w_2|)−1/6. Let ξ_r be the Gauss point |w_j|≤r. Near ξ_r the w-coordinates are invertible and define a degree-one coordinate torus. After translating log|w_j| by log r, regularize max(0,y_1,y_2) by H_ε=ε log(1+exp(y_1/ε)+exp(y_2/ε)). Its gradient is a diffeomorphism onto the open standard simplex, with inverse y_j=ε log(p_j/(1−p_1−p_2)). Change of variables gives ∫det D²H_ε=1/2. Scaling shows these measures concentrate at zero. The factorial normalization therefore gives 2 det D²H_ε dy→δ_0. Smooth analytic measures are carried by the w-coordinate Gauss section; its continuity and local uniform product convergence give the actual analytic atom δ_{ξ_r}. Thus its mass is exactly one, not merely a statement about a tropical pushforward. The remaining mass-one component is not identified.

Here |z_j(ξ_r)|=1 but |z_j−1|(ξ_r)=r<1; the canonical section's only point above zero is i(0), where |z_j−1|=1. Thus ξ_r is outside i(S). Furthermore D(i(0))=0 and D(ξ_r)=−1, so U does not factor through τ. This demonstrates movement of mass into analytic branches despite a skeleton-supported reference θ². It does not prove that every skeleton-supported equation has a noninvariant solution.

External setting and audit. Applied ordinary CLD inputs are precisely Theorem 15.7.1, the positive-current/order-zero and Radon correspondence in Section 7.2, Lemmas 8.5.1/8.5.3/8.5.5, recursive continuity/symmetry in 8.7, smooth-Hessian invariance in 8.8, and the degree/calibration integration definitions. Their immediate statements, proofs and hypotheses were read; restricted arguments are reconstructed above. Standard recursive analytic/differential foundations and their audit limits are disclosed in source-application-ledger.md. No full E¹ operator, analytic compactness/envelope theorem, or comparison with other psh classes follows. Full proofs are preserved in P16.7-paper.tex and whole-proof.md. Exact factorial and simplex checks appear in evidence/diagnostics.json; rerun with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`.

notes.summary: Solved every product-probability skeletal equation within a separable class, including energy, compactness and circle-envelope orthogonality. A rigid-point measure has restricted dual energy 1/6 but the restricted maximizer has the wrong MA measure.
notes.detailedSummary: For circle probabilities ν, h_ν=−G*ν uniquely solves dy+h''=ν modulo constants. Separable analytic potentials h_1∘τ_1+h_2∘τ_2 have genuine MA 2i_*(ν_1⊗ν_2), with uniqueness only within that class. Their energy equals the mixed CLD energy and admits exact first variation. Normalized compactness and one-dimensional obstacle orthogonality are proved. Restricted dual energy is finite for every positive analytic measure of mass two, but its maximizer depends only on coordinate marginals. For μ=2δ_(1,1), the restricted dual energy is exactly 1/6 and the maximizer has MA=2δ_i(0)≠μ. This disproves that proposed restricted all-support construction, not literal P16.7.
notes.text:
Use X, τ, i and the bounded genuine CLD operator from n1–n2. Let C=R/Z with Lebesgue probability dy, and H={h∈C⁰(C):ρ_h=dy+h'' is positive distributionally}. Testing against one shows that ρ_h has mass one. The periodic Green polynomial G(y)=y²/2−y/2+1/12 has mean zero, equal endpoint values, interior second derivative one and derivative jump −1 at zero. Hence G''=dy−δ_0.

Complete circle solution. For every Radon probability ν on C, h_ν(y)=−∫G(y−a)dν(a) is continuous, mean zero, and satisfies h_ν''=ν−dy. The difference of two solutions has zero distributional second derivative, so is affine on the line; periodicity makes it constant. Thus all members of H are given this way modulo constants. Since G ranges from −1/24 to 1/12 and is 1/2-Lipschitz, h_ν lies in [−1/12,1/24], is 1/2-Lipschitz and has oscillation at most 1/8. After sup h=0, the class lies in [−1/8,0]; Arzelà–Ascoli gives compactness, and positivity of dy+h'' is preserved under uniform limits.

Separable analytic equation. Put S_θ={h_1∘τ_1+h_2∘τ_2:h_j∈H}. Convex convolution of local weights gives S_θ⊂C_θ. For u=h_1+h_2 and v=k_1+k_2, the genuine mixed measure is α_u∧α_v=i_*(ρ_{h_1}⊗ρ_{k_2}+ρ_{k_1}⊗ρ_{h_2}). For smooth factors this follows from the diagonal Hessian and degree-one coordinate calibration. Periodic positive convolution converges uniformly in the functions and weakly in curvature probabilities, so the bounded CLD continuity from n2 proves the formula for every factor. In particular MA_θ(u)=2i_*(ρ_{h_1}⊗ρ_{h_2}). Every product measure 2i_*(ν_1⊗ν_2), for arbitrary circle Radon probabilities, is solved by h_{ν_1}+h_{ν_2}. Probability marginals recover each curvature measure, so uniqueness holds modulo constants within S_θ. No uniqueness among all analytic psh functions is asserted.

Energy and first variation. Define e(h)=∫h dy−(1/2)∫|h'|²dy and E_sep(u)=2(e(h_1)+e(h_2)). All derivatives are square integrable by the Lipschitz bound. This is independent of the choice of separable decomposition, and E_sep(u+c)=E_sep(u)+2c. It agrees with the genuine mixed CLD expression E(u)=(1/3)∫u(θ²+θ∧α_u+α_u²): inserting the mixed formula reduces this to Σ_j(∫h_j dy+∫h_j dρ_{h_j}), and periodic integration by parts gives ∫h_j dρ_{h_j}=∫h_j dy−∫|h_j'|²dy. Convolution justifies integration by parts for these Lipschitz functions, with derivatives converging in L² and curvature measures weakly.

The exact difference identity is e(k)−e(h)=∫(k−h)dρ_h−(1/2)∫|k'−h'|²dy. It proves strict concavity modulo constants and, along every separable segment, dE_sep(u+a(v−u))/da=∫(v−u)MA_θ(u+a(v−u)). These are separable directions only.

Restricted dual energy and an actual failure. For a positive analytic Radon measure μ of mass two, define E*_sep(μ)=sup_{u∈S_θ}(E_sep(u)−∫u dμ). Constants cancel. Normalize sup h_1=sup h_2=0; then −1/4≤u≤0 and E_sep(u)≤0. Thus 0≤E*_sep(μ)≤1/2 for every such μ. Let ν_j=(1/2)(τ_j)_*μ. The exact difference identity shows that the maximizer is h_{ν_1}+h_{ν_2}, unique modulo constants. Its MA is 2i_*(ν_1⊗ν_2), which generally differs from μ.

Take the actual rigid analytic point y represented by z_1=z_2=1 and μ=2δ_y. Both marginals are δ_0, so the maximizer is u_0=−G(x_1)−G(x_2). Its energy is −1/6 and u_0(y)=−1/6. The maximal objective, hence restricted dual energy, is exactly −1/6−2(−1/6)=1/6. But MA_θ(u_0)=2δ_{i(0)}≠2δ_y: at the rigid point |z_j−1|=0, whereas at i(0) it is one. This is a rigorous counterexample to all-support existence using S_θ and its restricted dual energy. It is not a counterexample to the original target: finite energy of this rigid-point measure in a correctly constructed full analytic cone is not established.

Complete circle-envelope argument. For continuous a:C→R, define P(a)=sup{h∈H:h≤a}. Constants below min a make the set nonempty. The common Lipschitz bound makes the supremum continuous; on the lifted line, y²/2+P(a) is the supremum of convex functions and is convex. Thus P(a)∈H and is the largest permitted function. Order and constant translation give ||P(a)−P(b)||∞≤||a−b||∞.

On an interval in {P(a)<a}, write F=y²/2+P(a). If F has curvature there, choose an arbitrarily short closed interval with positive obstacle clearance on which F is not affine. Replacing F by its endpoint chord raises it, preserves convexity because the chord slope lies between the outside one-sided slopes, and stays below the obstacle when the interval is sufficiently short. Repeat the replacement in every integer translate, preserving F(y+1)=F(y)+y+1/2. This contradicts maximality. Hence ρ_{P(a)} is supported on {P(a)=a}, proving ∫(a−P(a))dρ_{P(a)}=0.

For p=P(a), p_b=P(a+bv), the difference identity and contact identities yield b∫v dρ_{p_b}≤e(p_b)−e(p)≤b∫v dρ_p. Uniform Lipschitz continuity of P gives p_b→p uniformly, hence curvature probabilities converge weakly. Divide by b, reverse inequalities for b<0, and pass to the limit to obtain d e(P(a+bv))/db at zero=∫v dρ_p. These are circle envelopes; no envelope over all analytic θ-psh functions is identified with them.

Complete proofs are in P16.7-paper.tex and whole-proof.md. Evidence/diagnostics.json records exact Green normalizations, raw masses and 25 rational instances of the energy difference identity; these finite checks are independent of the universal distributional proofs. Reproduce with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`. This restricted endpoint does not construct the full analytic finite-energy domain or solve arbitrary-support P16.7.

notes.text:
Deliverables are in the authorized workspace /workspace/research/campaigns/round-264/P16.7-original-nonalgebraizable-finite-energy-equation/artifacts/codex-EI6X2Q: P16.7-paper.tex is the standalone full partial paper; whole-proof.md contains its complete mathematical body and every partial proof; source-application-ledger.md records exact applied statements, hypotheses, proof-reading coverage and missing primary evidence; scope-and-verdict.json preserves the original-completion verdict. README.md gives reproduction instructions. No imported note or historical acceptance label is used as a mathematical premise.

Literature observation, not an absence theorem. Public reconnaissance examined post-2020 analytic semipositivity, toric pluripotential theory, the 2026 balanced-polyhedral manuscript, and Kaib–Werner's 1 October 2026 abeloid-uniformization preprint. The authenticated supplied Gubler–Rabinoff v1 is arXiv:2503.05513v1, On semipositive piecewise linear functions in non-archimedean analytic geometry. Its analytic PL setting is distinct from the required finite-energy equation. BMPS's polyhedral theory and algebraic comparison examples do not automatically provide an all-support analytic lift. Genuine abeloid geometry likewise does not itself construct the requested MA theory. No inspected statement supplied the whole original theorem; search coverage is finite. A final attempted GR v2 HTML URL returned 404, so that attempt authenticates no later version.

The unchanged original task and three manifests were read first and preserved. Entire applied CLD-v2 text/PDF and the whole supplied GR-v1 text/PDF are retained in sources/. Retrieval responses and actual CLD page images are in evidence/. Applied CLD immediate statements and proofs were inspected with their definitions and mass conventions. Recursive published Berkovich/CLD foundations are disclosed rather than silently treated as newly proved. The complete referenced torus classification/ampleness book proofs were not retrieved; therefore n1 does not certify actual nonalgebraizability. The public tool worked, although the inherited shell proxy was unreachable and some full-book requests failed. Network/auth/proxy/CA settings were unchanged.

Execution evidence. Run, in this directory, `python scripts/prepare_evidence.py`, `python scripts/diagnostics.py`, then `python scripts/build_artifacts.py`. The first requires the preserved immutable parent packet and copies eight authorized input/source files. The diagnostic uses only the Python standard library and exact fractions: 41 checks passed; all 6,561 tuples in [-4,4]^4 were examined, with nine symmetry solutions. Other checks covered Green-function identities, the factorial/simplex normalization and bounded energy identities. Artifact checks found balanced lexical braces, environments and display delimiters, eight numbered statements and six formal proof environments. The complete companion was generated from the full paper body. Outputs, environment, commands and SHA-256 inventory are preserved. These are finite calculations and lexical checks, not mathematical certification. TeX was not compiled under the user's ROOT-only compilation restriction. No supplied program, extra agent/model call, heavy computation, external message or external state change was used.

Original verdict. Results n1–n3 establish the stated partial construction, bounded products/comparison, an actual branch perturbation, and an explicitly restricted equation/energy/envelope theory. Missing original quantifiers are: exclusion of every algebraization; an intrinsic full analytic psh cone and full E¹ domain; unbounded mixed products with full mass and decreasing continuity; the correct full dual-energy condition; compactness and envelopes over the full analytic cone; orthogonality and first variation in every analytic direction; existence for every admissible measure with arbitrary analytic support; and uniqueness modulo constants throughout the full domain. Neither restricted counterexample disproves literal P16.7. No other atomic target is claimed solved, and original P16.7 completion is false.
